candidate.name: Landing or takeoff on an unintended surface
candidate.definition: The aircraft lands, lines up to land, or starts a takeoff on a surface other than the assigned runway: a taxiway, a closed or wrong runway, or the wrong airport.

supporting_reports.evidence: During a night visual approach to Runway 27R the crew lined up on the parallel taxiway, mistaking the taxiway edge lights for runway lights.
Cleared for takeoff on Runway 4L, the crew taxied onto Runway 4R, which was closed for construction.
The crew landed at a nearby general aviation airport with a similar runway alignment instead of the destination airport.
After a late runway change the crew did not rebrief the approach and landed on Runway 35L instead of the assigned Runway 35R.
In low visibility the crew began a takeoff from taxiway Bravo, believing it was the runway.

candidate.name: Runway entry or crossing without clearance
candidate.definition: An aircraft or vehicle crosses a hold-short line, stop bar or holding point and enters an active runway without a clearance.

supporting_reports.evidence: The stop bar lights were on, but the crew continued past the holding point onto the runway after mistaking a frequency change for a crossing clearance.
A readback error led the crew to hear cross Runway 9 instead of hold short of Runway 9, and the aircraft entered the active runway without a clearance.
Taxiing to Runway 16, the crew crossed the hold-short line for Runway 22 without a clearance while another aircraft was on its takeoff roll.
A snow removal vehicle entered the active runway without a clearance during clearing operations.

candidate.name: Overrun after a long or fast landing on a wet or contaminated runway
candidate.definition: The aircraft touches down long or fast on a wet or contaminated runway, braking is poor, and it overruns the runway end.

supporting_reports.evidence: Braking action was poor and the aircraft overran the runway end by 60 metres into the runway end safety area.
With one thrust reverser unavailable, a long landing on a contaminated runway ended in a low-speed overrun past the runway end.
After an unstabilized, fast approach the aircraft touched down 2,500 feet beyond the threshold on a runway reported with standing water and came to a stop in the overrun area.

diag.candidate: Overrun after a long or fast landing on a wet or contaminated runway

definitions.body: An aircraft departs the runway surface during the takeoff or landing roll, including overruns after a long or fast landing.

definitions.body: A runway condition code from 6 (dry) down to 0 reports braking performance on wet or contaminated runways (water, slush, snow, ice), so crews can recompute landing distance.
An aircraft leaves the runway surface during takeoff or landing, either by veering off the side or by overrunning the end.

candidate.name: TCAS resolution advisory after an altitude deviation
candidate.definition: The aircraft deviates from its cleared altitude (level bust) and traffic receives a TCAS resolution advisory or separation is lost.

supporting_reports.evidence: The resulting level bust triggered a TCAS climb resolution advisory and separation was lost.
The climbing aircraft overshot its cleared altitude of FL240 by 400 feet, and opposite-direction traffic received a TCAS resolution advisory to descend.
Autopilot mode confusion caused an altitude deviation, and the crew received a TCAS resolution advisory for traffic 600 feet below.
The controller issued a descent clearance into conflicting traffic and both aircraft received TCAS resolution advisories.

candidate.name: Clear-air turbulence with cabin injuries
candidate.definition: An unexpected encounter with turbulence in clear air injures passengers or cabin crew who are standing, unbelted or near unsecured carts.

supporting_reports.evidence: Moderate to severe clear-air turbulence over the mountains caught the cabin with carts not secured, and a flight attendant was struck by a cart.

Unforecast turbulence near the jet stream occurred just after the seat belt sign was turned off.

candidate.name: Engine damage or shutdown after bird ingestion
candidate.definition: Birds ingested into an engine cause vibration, surge, loss of thrust, fire warning or shutdown.

supporting_reports.evidence: After ingesting a large bird at 3,000 feet the crew received an engine fire warning, shut the engine down and discharged the fire extinguisher.
The engine vibrated and lost thrust, and the crew shut it down and returned.
Multiple bird strikes during the takeoff roll caused the right engine to surge, and the crew rejected the takeoff.
